cases.name: Yhoana Arteaga
cases.about: She was a seventh-grade student at Nashville’s Liberty Collegiate Academy. Friends and family described her as kind, polite, caring, fun, intelligent and beautiful.
cases.narrative: She was found dead in her bedroom after being beaten and strangled, allegedly with a karate belt.

cases.name: Barbara Barnes Pitts
cases.about:
“She is often credited as the person that drove the spirit and the culture of our company because she is… you know… the kind of person that you meet and you immediately feel better about yourself? Comfortable? That is her,” described Barrett Ward, CEO and Founder of ABLE, where Barbara worked. Barbara was known as an innovator. Ward described how she grew the jewelry department from one person to 20 during her time with the company.

cases.name: Karlie Rashell Yellin Judge
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Karlie spent the first 10 years of her life in Rhode Island before moving to Maryland. Like her parents, she embarked on many journeys in her young life. From Columbia, MD to Surfside Beach, SC, to Asheville, NC, and finally settling in Goodlettsville, TN.

Karlie was known for her soft and caring demeanor, love for baking, and being a mother to her cat, Ali Cat."
cases.narrative: On 5/17/2023, her body was found during a welfare check.
